turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You gave my son a zero without calling me, Hale. I want to know why.
I entered the zero before calling you. That was my mistake, and I own it.
Okay. On what basis?
Here's the version history. Created October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. 612 words at 11:52, 794 more at 11:58, then 23 minutes of formatting. No earlier drafts.
Let me see that screen. He could have drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in. And did anyone ask Owen before that zero went in?
And his outline argued cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay. Show me the outline, with its date. And you still haven't told me whether Owen was heard before you entered that zero.
Procedure 4.4 allows a private supervised rewrite. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
Allows. Are you offering it, in writing, tonight? And for the third time, was Owen heard first?
Can I ask you a few questions about Owen's habits at home?
I'm not the one being questioned, Hale. Was he heard first, and are you putting that rewrite in writing?
Does he usually work late?
His home isn't on the table. You've dodged my question three times now, and I'm keeping count.
Does anyone help him with his homework?
No. If your next sentence isn't an answer, I'm walking down to the principal's office.
You keep not answering me.
Not answering you. I'm not the one on trial in this room. Yes or no: did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?
So the rewrite is agreed?
Nothing's agreed. You said allows, not that you're offering it in writing, and you still haven't answered me.
Are you sure you're okay with it?
That's a leading question, and I'm not answering it. Answer mine.
I just want to be clear on the terms.
Ten minutes. Clear is this: nothing goes on his record, this stays quiet, and you tell me whether Owen was heard before the zero.
Can you say them back to me one more time?
I've said it once. You can write it down, and then you can answer me.
And you won't change your mind tonight?
Not on a question with no answer attached.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that nothing is placed on Owen's record, that this stays private, and that you tell me in writing whether Owen was spoken to before the zero was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She got to her fallback position and still wants a firm commitment, in writing, that nothing goes on his record and this stays private, plus a straight answer on whether Owen was heard first; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was within reach but never committed to, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling home in one sentence and moved on, which took away her first grievance and earned the only ground she gave.
What cost ground: You kept dodging her question about whether Owen was heard before the zero and switched to questions about his home life, which looked like you were building a case against him rather than following your own procedure.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed very close to that, showing the essay appearing between about 11:30 PM and midnight on October 28, the night before it was due, and your question about him working late pressed on it too; that proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said he could have drafted it elsewhere and pasted it in, answer that with something she can check, tell her plainly whether you spoke to Owen, and then commit to the 4.4 rewrite in writing with a date before December 1.
